Wien's displacement law (λ_max = b/T) for a temperature of 6500 K gives a peak wavelength of approximately 446 nm, which is in the blue region of the visible spectrum. Since the star is moving away from Earth, its light is subject to the Doppler effect, causing a redshift, which is a shift towards longer, redder wavelengths.
